guidance: Reference data that has to exist before any transaction can use it; it usually comes first on a level and is done by an administrator or a specialist rather than the person running the transaction
example: Warranty Term; Action Plan Template; Advanced Account Forecast Set

guidance: The main business record of the capability: the thing people talk about (an agreement; a claim; a visit; a fleet). Its creation usually starts the core of the level; any object with no other match is treated as one
Detail rows under a master record (lines; schedules; items). They follow their master and are often one step with it when there are few
example: Sales Agreement Product; Claim Item; Shipment Item

guidance: Junction records that connect the master to accounts; contacts; assets or other records. Usually a step after the master exists; name the step after the business purpose (identify claim participants) rather than the junction
example: Claim Participant; Fleet Asset; Asset Warranty

guidance: Things that happen to records over time (movements; state changes; adjustments; requests). They sit in the middle or late part of the level and often carry the decisions and loops
example: Product Item Transaction; Product Transfer; Account Forecast Adjustment

guidance: Numbers derived from the other records (forecasts; targets; KPIs). They usually come last on a level and feed a review or monitoring step
example: Advanced Account Forecast Fact; Account Manager Target; Generic Visit Key Performance Indicator
